exposure: Mode of delivery (Caesarean section, vaginal delivery, assisted vaginal delivery)
cohort: Women in Denmark who gave birth to liveborn, singleton babies between January 1, 1997, and December 31, 2015 (3255 women with IBD and 207,608 without IBD who had a caesarean section; 5771 women with IBD and 793,110 women without IBD who had a vaginal delivery)
finding: Women with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) have an increased risk of 30-day postpartum infectious complications, particularly gastrointestinal and skin infections, regardless of delivery mode.
mod_finding: The risk of a 30-day postpartum infectious complication is increased in women with IBD who have a caesarean section or a vaginal delivery.
